page: Microsoft Azure EC8as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage capabilities for persistent data. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not present. Across CPU and memory evaluation suites, the EC8as_v5 consistently scores within the middle 50 percent benchmark tier. It achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1202.0 and a multi-core score of 4658.0, alongside stress-ng results of 1989.26 for single-core and 7920.99 for multi-core compute throughput.

In operational testing, the instance delivered 6.75 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and reached a PassMark database operations metric of 2864.68. The balanced memory subsystem and dedicated core allocation deliver predictable performance for data-intensive processing without paying a premium for unused GPU hardware. However, applications requiring low-latency scratch disks must account for the lack of local temporary NVMe storage.

Given its high RAM-to-CPU ratio and stable benchmark profile, the EC8as_v5 is suited for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational databases, medium-scale enterprise resource planning software, and distributed data analytics workloads.

It excludes integrated local storage and GPU acceleration, directing I/O demands to external Premium Storage volumes. Performance benchmarks place the EC8as_v5 in the middle tier across standard compute and memory tests, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4658.0, a PassMark CPU score of 9071.03, and Redis throughput exceeding 6.75 million operations per second. The hardware configuration emphasizes cost efficiency by pairing dedicated compute with dense memory capacity, foregoing specialized accelerators. This profile makes it practical for in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, and memory-bound transactional systems.
